title: Developing the theory of formative assessment
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the question of how to build a clearer theory of formative assessment and how to situate formative feedback within broader theories of pedagogy and learning. The authors argue that formative assessment had previously been described through lists of practices, but that a stronger conceptual basis was needed to explain how those practices fit together and how they support learning.

The paper develops a framework that defines formative assessment as the elicitation, interpretation, and use of evidence about student achievement by teachers, learners, or peers to make better-founded instructional decisions. It organizes formative assessment into five strategies: clarifying learning intentions and success criteria, engineering classroom discussions and tasks that elicit evidence, providing feedback that moves learning forward, activating students as resources for one another, and activating students as owners of their own learning. The authors connect this framework to self-regulated learning, classroom discourse, cognitive acceleration, and dynamic assessment, and discuss how feedback decisions depend on interpreting learner responses and matching them to instructional goals.

The context is broad classroom teaching rather than a single empirical study: the paper draws on prior literature from school settings, including examples from science and mathematics classrooms, to show how formative practices operate in everyday instruction. The main conclusion is that formative assessment should be understood as contingent interaction that regulates learning, and that stronger theoretical models can help teachers implement feedback more effectively and avoid superficial adoption of isolated techniques.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a theoretical/review paper on formative assessment, not an empirical evaluation of a technology or AI intervention. It is peer-reviewed academic work, but it does not present a study design with primary outcome data for the requested taxonomy.
impact_tier_rationale: No direct intervention impact is measured in this paper, so there is no empirical effect to classify. The paper is influential conceptually for formative assessment, but it does not provide outcome evidence for K-12 science learning or any technology-based support.
